figures.caption: Secondary structure characterization of AMPs. 3D structural model prediction of (A) S-4, (B) L-4, and (C) P-4; the red sections represent 1–4, and the yellow sections represent the Pseudomonas, S. aureus, and Lactobacillus monocytogenes pheromones. figures.caption: Bactericidal activity of AMPs. Survival rates and agar plates photographs of (A) E. coli, (B) MDR-E. coli, (C) MDR-A. baumannii, and (D) MDR-E. faecalis treated with 1–4, S-4, L-4, and P-4 (2, 4, 6 μg/mL) or Amcill-s or Kana-s (6 μg/mL). Data are presented as mean ± SD (n = 3); * means p < 0.05, ** means p < 0.01, *** means p < 0.001, **** means p < 0.0001, and ns means no significant difference.

figures.caption: Antibiofilm activity of AMPs. (A) Photographs and (B) membrane quality quantification of crystal violet stained E. coli and MDR-E. coli biofilms treated with 1–4, S-4, L-4, and P-4 (48 μg/mL) or Amcill-s or Kana-s (48 μg/mL). Data are presented as mean ± SD (n = 3); **** means p < 0.0001. (C) Confocal images of Calcein-AM/PI-stained E. coli and MDR-E. coli biofilms treated with 1–4, S-4, L-4, and P-4 (48 μg/mL) or Amcill-s or Kana-s (48 μg/mL). (Red: PI, excitation wavelength is 535 nm, emission wavelength is 615 nm; Green: Calcein, excitation wavelength 494 nm, emission wavelength 514 nm). Scale bar: 50 μm.
